title: Entropy mapping under uniaxial pressure utilizing the elastocaloric effect
authors: Zhenhai Hu, You-Sheng Li, Aleksei V. Frolov, Fabian Jerzembeck, Manuel Brando, Naoki Kikugawa, Dmitry A. Sokolov, Hilary M. L. Noad, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Michael Nicklas, Andreas W. Rost
abstract: Uniaxial pressure is a powerful tuning parameter for quantum materials, but conventional thermodynamic probes such as specific heat are difficult to realize in the constrained geometries of strain apparatus. We develop a quantitative analysis framework for a.c. elastocaloric effect measurements that enable the reconstruction of the absolute entropy and hence specific heat across complex phase diagrams. The absolute accuracy is achieved by combining measurements in the strong coupling regime at low frequencies with high signal-to-noise measurements in the quasi-adiabatic regime at high frequencies. Applying the approach to the correlated superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, we obtain an absolute entropy map across the phase diagram including across phase transitions deep into the superconducting state. We demonstrate that from such data one can derive the absolute specific heat which is currently not possible through other approaches. This data reinforces the finding that the quenching of entropy within the superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ is strongest at the critical strain consistent with the superconducting gap being maximized at the Van Hove singularity (VHs). Furthermore, we demonstrate that, although $Δc /(γT) $ does increase at the VH strain, this increase is much weaker than previously inferred from more indirect caloric experiments.
summary: This work introduces a novel method using the a.c. elastocaloric effect to map the absolute entropy and specific heat of quantum materials like $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ under uniaxial strain. By combining low- and high-frequency measurements, the authors overcome limitations of traditional probes. The results provide quantitative evidence regarding entropy changes across superconducting and magnetic phase transitions in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: To develop a quantitative framework to reconstruct absolute entropy and specific heat across complex phase diagrams of quantum materials under uniaxial pressure, overcoming limitations of conventional thermodynamic probes.
main_result: The method successfully maps the absolute entropy and specific heat for $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$, showing that entropy quenching is strongest at the critical strain corresponding to the Van Hove singularity.
method: The analysis combines measurements from the low-frequency (strong coupling) and high-frequency (quasi-adiabatic) regimes of the a.c. elastocaloric effect to achieve absolute accuracy in entropy reconstruction.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the correlated superconductor $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ subjected to uniaxial strain. The theoretical framework uses the entropy balance equation to relate heat flow from an external heater to the elastocaloric response.
key_observables: Absolute entropy map, specific heat ($c/T$), and the temperature oscillation amplitude ($	ilde{T}_s$) as a function of strain and frequency.
important_parameters: Uniaxial strain ($\varepsilon$), temperature ($T$), and measurement frequency ($\omega$), with characteristic time scales set by $	au_1 = C_{	ext{tot}}/k$.
main_assumptions: The reconstruction relies on combining data from two distinct frequency regimes (low vs. high) and treating the elastocaloric response as an effective heat source in the thermodynamic balance equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram of $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ under strain, the experimental setup, and plots comparing the normalized temperature oscillation signal ($	ilde{T}_s$) across different frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving the governing differential equation unifying heating and elastocaloric effects. It then applies this framework to $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ to map the entropy and specific heat across its superconducting and magnetic phase boundaries.
why_interesting: The ability to probe absolute thermodynamic quantities like entropy and specific heat deep within the superconducting state using strain-induced effects provides a powerful, non-invasive tool for characterizing strongly correlated electron systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic temperature–strain phase diagram of Sr2RuO4 as a function of compressive strain ε, along the ⟨100⟩ crystal axis. The superconducting (SC) dome is enhanced in the vicinity of the strain-tuned Van Hove singularity (VHs) at εVHs [12], separating the low-temperature superconducting phase from the normal-state which at low strains is well de- scribed by standard Fermi liquid theory. At larger compres- sive strain, a magnetically ordered (M) phase emerges [16]. At εVHs, the increased darker shading denotes an enhanced density of states.

FIG. 2. Experimental setup and basic thermal model for heat-capacity and elastocaloric effect measurements. (a) Photograph of the experimental setup with the principal components annotated. An Au/AuFe thermocouple and a resistive heater are thermally coupled to the sample using silver epoxy, while the sample is mechanically anchored to titanium plates with epoxy resin. (b) Schematic diagram of the setup, emphasizing the spatial arrangement and thermal connections between the sample, heater, thermocouple, and strain cell. The blue curve shows the analytical result given by Eq. 1, while the orange curve corresponds to a numerical simulation incor- porating a more realistic experimental thermal model. Both are plotted as functions of the dimensionless drive frequency ω/ω1, where ω1 is defined in text.
